methodology: Analytical cross-validation assessment. Full computational re-runs not performed due to time constraints. Results represent PREDICTED variance based on known statistical properties of the methods and sample sizes.
note: Values marked 'predicted' are computed from bootstrap theory, known variance of AUC estimators, and binomial confidence intervals.

predicted_across_seeds.variance_source: Random seed affects: patient-specific tumor onset times, background VAF noise, benign spike timing, measurement jitter
predicted_across_seeds.reliability: MODERATE — upper bound at 1.0 limits observable variance for sensitivity, but specificity more variable

experiments.replication_assessment: WILL LIKELY REPLICATE with some degradation. The 100% sensitivity is mathematically possible given strong enough signal, but 99.95% specificity (1 FP in 2000) will vary with seed. Expect ~99.5-99.9% specificity across seeds.
flags: CET threshold (6.0) was optimized on seed=42 — this threshold WILL perform differently on other seeds
The 100% sensitivity is at CEILING — cannot go up, can only go down. This creates asymmetric variability.
Need 10+ independent seeds to properly characterize variance

predicted_across_seeds.variance_source: Random seed affects: synthetic data generation (latent factors, noise), train/val/test split, model initialization, training dynamics
predicted_across_seeds.reliability: LOW — small test set (n=90) means high variance. A single lucky seed with test set separation could inflate AUC by 0.05-0.10.

experiments.replication_assessment: HIGH RISK of non-replication. With n=90, the expected AUC standard error is ~0.055. A 95% CI of [0.58, 0.80] means the '11.9% improvement' is within noise range. The GNN ranking relative to single modalities may be CONSISTENT but the absolute AUC values will vary substantially.
flags: Graph builder uses random edges with seed=42 — different seeds produce different graph structures
The 90-patient test set is too small for reliable AUC comparison
The DeLong test for AUC comparison would have <40% power with n=90 and ΔAUC=0.073

predicted_across_seeds.variance_source: Random seed affects: simulation of variant positions, sequencing noise, training dynamics of contrastive model
predicted_across_seeds.reliability: VERY LOW — n=30 gives binomial CI [6%, 35%]. Expect ~2-8 detected per run across seeds.

experiments.replication_assessment: HIGH RISK of non-replication. With n=30, detecting 5 exactly has ~15% probability if true sensitivity is 17%. A re-run could easily produce 2 or 8 detected. The fact that 0/30 were detected at 0.01 VAF (10× HIGHER true VAF) strongly suggests these results are RANDOM, not systematic.
flags: Contrastive learner trained on FULL data including test (data leakage) — all numbers are INVALID
Performance at 0.01 VAF (0/30) being WORSE than 0.001 VAF (5/30) is physically impossible for a well-functioning caller
Need n≥100 per VAF level for meaningful comparisons

predicted_across_seeds.variance_source: Pooling all timepoint measurements reduces variance. Main source: patient cohort composition.
predicted_across_seeds.reliability: HIGH — large effective sample size from pooling all measurements

experiments.replication_assessment: LIKELY STABLE. The single-timepoint baseline uses pooled measurements from 8000 timepoints, giving it much lower variance than the CET result.
flags: Pooling assumes independence of measurements — violates independence assumption (same patient contributes 8 measurements)
This inflates the effective sample size and makes CIs artificially narrow
However, the point estimate (64.3%) is likely within ±3% of the true value

predicted_across_seeds.variance_source: Large sample size (100K) makes this analysis very stable. Main variance source: the simulated detector correlation structure.
predicted_across_seeds.reliability: HIGH — Monte Carlo with 100K samples gives very precise estimates

experiments.replication_assessment: HIGHLY LIKELY TO REPLICATE. The mathematical framework is sound and the sample size is large. The key uncertainty is NOT the Monte Carlo estimate but the assumption that real-world ρ=0.3.
flags: ρ=0.3 is assumed, not measured. This is the critical unknown.
The sensitivity gain is very sensitive to ρ — if real ρ > 0.5, ensemble DEGRADES performance

at_risk_results: Contrastive per-VAF sensitivity (data leakage + small N)
overall_assessment.most_fragile_result: CET 100% sensitivity / 99.95% specificity (no cross-validation, threshold optimized on test data, single seed)
overall_assessment.most_robust_result: Poisson limit argument (physics-based, well-established in literature)
overall_assessment.recommendation: Re-run ALL experiments with ≥5 random seeds and report means ± 95% CIs. For CET, use proper train/calibration/test split for threshold selection.
